title: Little Office of S. Francis Borgia of the Society of Jesus
translationNotice: English translation prepared for Sacrum Florilegium; not supplied in the source PDF.

blocks.source: Narrabo nomen tuum fratribus meis: in medio Ecclesiae laudabo te.
blocks.english: I shall tell Thy name to my brethren; in the midst of the Church I shall praise Thee.

blocks.source: ℣. Domine, labia mea aperies.
blocks.english: ℣. O Lord, Thou shalt open my lips.

blocks.source: ℟. Et os meum annuntiabit laudem tuam.
blocks.english: ℟. And my mouth shall declare Thy praise.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus, in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri, et Filio, et Spiritui Sancto. Sicut erat in principio, et nunc, et semper, et in saecula saeculorum. Amen.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Illustre sidus Principum, Francisce salve maxime; Qui foetido cadavere Viso, horruisti saeculum.
blocks.english: Hail, great Francis, illustrious star of princes, who, seeing a putrid corpse, recoiled from the world.

blocks.source: Averte nostra lumina, Ne vanitates hauriant, Sed in supernam caelitum Sint fixa saeculum jugiter.
blocks.english: Turn our eyes away, lest they drink in vanities; may they remain ever fixed upon the heavenly age of heaven’s citizens.

blocks.source: Antiphona
blocks.english: Antiphon

blocks.source: Taeduit me vitae meae, videns me mala universae sub sole, et cohorruit aeternitas vanitatem et afflictionem spiritus.
blocks.english: I grew weary of my life, seeing all the evils beneath the sun, and eternity shuddered at vanity and affliction of spirit.
blocks.editorialNote: The PDF prints the irregular antiphon “videns me mala ... cohorruit aeternitas vanitatem.” The prepared English retains the literal unusual eternity imagery rather than replacing this with a standard biblical passage.

blocks.source: ℣. Non aspiciam hominem ultra, et habitatorum quietis.
blocks.english: ℣. I shall no longer look upon man, nor upon those who dwell at rest.

blocks.source: ℟. Haec requies mea in saeculum saeculi: quoniam elegi eam.
blocks.english: ℟. This is my rest for ever and ever, for I have chosen it.

blocks.source: Oremus,
blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: Omnipotens, sempiterne Deus, qui spreta vanitate, beatum Franciscum Borgiam et Societatem Filii tui vocare dignatus es: praesta, quaesumus, ut, quem eximia sanctimoniae exempla par habuimus in terris, ejus coronae participes fieri mereamur in caelis. Per Christum Dominum nostrum. Amen.
blocks.english: Almighty and everlasting God, who didst deign to call Blessed Francis Borgia, despising vanity, into the Society of Thy Son, grant, we beseech Thee, that we who had him upon earth as an outstanding example of holiness may be found worthy to share his crown in heaven. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
blocks.editorialNote: The PDF prints “et Societatem” and “exempla par habuimus.” The prepared English provisionally understands a call into the Society and an example of holiness; the printed Latin remains.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri, et Filio, et Spiritui Sancto.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Salve columna Gandiae, Et Religionis gloria: Qui aula relicta Principis, Aulam petisti Numinis.
blocks.english: Hail, pillar of Gandia and glory of religious life, who, leaving the prince’s court, sought the court of God.

blocks.source: Servos fideles caelitum Servire fac nos Principi, Ut tecum eodem praemio Perfruamur perpetuo.
blocks.english: Make us faithful servants of the Prince of heaven, that with thee we may enjoy the same reward for ever.

blocks.source: Antiphona
blocks.english: Antiphon

blocks.source: Coacervavi mihi argentum, et aurum, et substantias Regum et Provinciarum: vidi in omnibus vanitatem, et afflictionem animi, et nihil permanere sub sole.
blocks.english: I heaped up for myself silver and gold and the wealth of kings and provinces; I saw vanity in all things and affliction of soul, and that nothing endures beneath the sun.

blocks.source: ℣. Beatus vir, qui timet Dominum:
blocks.english: ℣. Blessed is the man who feareth the Lord,

blocks.source: ℟. Et non respexit in vanitates, et insanias falsas.
blocks.english: ℟. And hath not looked upon vanities and false follies.

blocks.source: Oratio ut supra.
blocks.english: Prayer as above.

blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Salve, o speculum pauperum, Opumque spretor inclite, Felicitatem divitum Qui vanitatem duxeras:
blocks.english: Hail, mirror of the poor and renowned despiser of riches, who counted the happiness of the wealthy as vanity.

blocks.source: Fac spiritu nos pauperes, Virtute vero divites, Gazas caducas spernere, Solumque Christum quaerere.
blocks.english: Make us poor in spirit but rich in virtue, to despise perishable treasures and seek Christ alone.

blocks.source: Antiphona
blocks.english: Antiphon

blocks.source: Coacervavi mihi argentum, et aurum, et substantias Regum et Provinciarum: vidi in omnibus vanitatem, et afflictionem animi, et nihil permanere sub sole.
blocks.english: I heaped up for myself silver and gold and the wealth of kings and provinces; I saw vanity in all things and affliction of soul, and that nothing endures beneath the sun.

blocks.source: ℣. Beatus vir, cujus est nomen Domini spes ejus.
blocks.english: ℣. Blessed is the man whose hope is the name of the Lord,

blocks.source: ℟. Et non respexit in vanitates, et insanias falsas.
blocks.english: ℟. And hath not looked upon vanities and false follies.

blocks.source: Oratio ut supra.
blocks.english: Prayer as above.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Salve polaris flammula, Caeli voluptas, Borgia, Devotionis lachryma Cui madebant lumina:
blocks.english: Hail, little flame of heaven’s pole, Borgia, delight of heaven, whose eyes were wet with tears of devotion.

blocks.source: Rores supernos gratiae Devotionis depule, Cor incalescat frigidum, Flammis amoris affluat.
blocks.english: Shed upon us heavenly dews of grace and devotion; may the cold heart grow warm and abound in flames of love.
blocks.editorialNote: The PDF prints “depule,” where the context appears to intend “deplue” (rain down). The prepared English provisionally renders “shed upon us”; the printed verb remains for editorial resolution.

blocks.source: Antiphona
blocks.english: Antiphon

blocks.source: Cor suum tradet ad vigilandum diluculo ad Dominum, qui fecit illum:
blocks.english: He will give his heart to keep watch at dawn for the Lord who made him,

blocks.source: et in conspectu Altissimi deprecabitur.
blocks.english: And he will pray before the Most High.

blocks.source: ℣. Tanquam imbres mittet eloquia sapientiae tuae.
blocks.english: ℣. He shall send forth the words of Thy wisdom like showers,

blocks.source: ℟. Et in oratione constituitur Domino.
blocks.english: ℟. And in prayer he is established before the Lord.

blocks.source: Oratio ut supra.
blocks.english: Prayer as above.

blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Salve pudicitiae rosa, Et castitatis lilium: Hostis voluptae maxime, Carnisque victor hostium:
blocks.english: Hail, rose of modesty and lily of chastity, greatest enemy of pleasure and conqueror of the foes of the flesh.

blocks.source: Tu puritatem corporis, Mentisque serves integram: Cor munda ab omni crimine, Dignus thorus sit Numine.
blocks.english: Preserve the purity of our body and mind intact; cleanse the heart from every sin, that it may be a bridal chamber worthy of God.

blocks.source: Antiphona
blocks.english: Antiphon

blocks.source: O quam pulchra et casta generatio cum claritate: immortalis est enim memoria illius: quoniam apud Deum nota est, et apud homines.
blocks.english: O how beautiful is a chaste generation with glory! Its memory is immortal, for it is known before God and men.

blocks.source: ℣. Retribuet mihi Dominus secundum justitiam meam.
blocks.english: ℣. The Lord shall reward me according to my righteousness,

blocks.source: ℟. Et secundum puritatem manuum mearum in conspectu oculorum ejus.
blocks.english: ℟. And according to the purity of my hands in the sight of His eyes.

blocks.source: Oratio ut supra.
blocks.english: Prayer as above.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Salve culmen humilium, Exemplum obedientiae, Calcata honoris purpura, Demissionis gratia.
blocks.english: Hail, summit of the humble, example of obedience, who trod underfoot the purple of honour through the grace of self-abasement.

blocks.source: Qui claruit maxima, Motus superbos comprime, Mentes rebelles doma, Humilesque veros effice.
blocks.english: Thou who wast greatly renowned, restrain proud impulses; tame rebellious minds and make us truly humble.

blocks.source: Antiphona
blocks.english: Antiphon

blocks.source: Sapientiam humilitati exaltabit caput illius, in medio Magnatum considerare illum faciet.
blocks.english: Wisdom shall exalt his head for humility, and make him take his place amid the great.
blocks.editorialNote: The PDF prints the irregular “Sapientiam humilitati ... considerare.” The prepared English provisionally understands wisdom exalting the humble man and placing him among the great; the printed Latin remains.

blocks.source: ℣. Memoriam superborum perdidit Deus.
blocks.english: ℣. God hath destroyed the memory of the proud,

blocks.source: ℟. Reliquit memoriam humilium sensu.
blocks.english: ℟. He hath left the memory of the humble in mind.

blocks.source: Oratio ut supra.
blocks.english: Prayer as above.

referenceExpansion.note: Collect printed in full at Matins in this same office.

blocks.source: ℣. Converte nos Deus salutaris noster.
blocks.english: ℣. Convert us, O God our Saviour.

blocks.source: ℟. Et averte iram tuam a nobis.
blocks.english: ℟. And turn away Thine anger from us.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri, et Filio, et Spiritui Sancto.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Salve potestas daemonum, Bellator invincibilis, Qui nobilis victoriae Plaudens migrasti e corpore.
blocks.english: Hail, power against demons, invincible warrior, who, rejoicing in a noble victory, didst depart from the body.
blocks.editorialNote: The printed “potestas daemonum” can literally mean power of demons. In the address to the saint the prepared English provisionally understands power against demons; this relation remains for editorial resolution.

blocks.source: Adversus infernalium Tentationes hostium, Nobis adis fortissimum In morte propugnaculum.
blocks.english: Against the temptations of infernal foes, be for us a mighty defence in death.
blocks.editorialNote: The PDF prints “Nobis adis fortissimum” without a clear verb of giving or being. The English provisionally understands a request for a strong defence at death; the Latin remains.

blocks.source: Antiphona
blocks.english: Antiphon

blocks.source: Justus, si morte praeoccupatus fuerit, in refrigerio erit. Senectus enim venerabilis est, non diuturna, nec numero annorum numerata computata.
blocks.english: The righteous man, if overtaken by death, shall be at rest. For venerable old age is not long duration, nor reckoned by the counted number of years.

blocks.source: ℣. Gloriosa in conspectu Domini.
blocks.english: ℣. Glorious in the sight of the Lord,

blocks.source: ℟. Mors Sanctorum ejus.
blocks.english: ℟. Is the death of His saints.
blocks.editorialNote: English reused from an identical complete Latin passage elsewhere in this PDF. This office’s source transcription still requires its own review.

blocks.source: Oratio ut supra.
blocks.english: Prayer as above.

editorialNotes.text: English prepared after visual comparison with PDF pages 498–500. The six repeated collects expand from Matins; only the seven printed hours are offered, with no Lauds added. Printed grammatical defects and possible verb transposition are noted inline and keep the source pending.
